name: Bardia National Park Safari

difficulty.notes: Full-day jungle walks (tiger tracking) are long, hot and on foot in tiger/elephant habitat; jeep safaris are easy.

duration_days.notes: Three nights in Thakurdwara is the common minimum; a 4th night adds a second tiger-tracking session or a Babai Valley day. Often combined with Chitwan or Lumbini.

itinerary.route: Kathmandu - Nepalgunj (flight ~1 h) - Thakurdwara (drive ~2.5-3 h, ~95 km); Tharu village walk / park HQ visit
Full-day guided jungle walk / tiger tracking along Karnali riverbanks and grassland machans (watchtowers)
itinerary.notes: Licensed nature guides lead walks; tiger sightings are never guaranteed.

itinerary.route: Full-day jeep safari; Karnali river boat/canoe trip for Gangetic dolphin and gharial

best_seasons.notes: NTB: Oct-Mar best; Apr-Jun hot/dry (up to 42 C); Jul-Sep rainy. Operators report the hot dry months (Mar-May) give the best tiger odds as grass is cut/burnt and animals gather at water - operator claim.

permits.name: Bardia National Park entry permit
permits.applies_to: foreign nationals; SAARC NPR 750; Nepali NPR 100; under 10 free

guide_requirements: Entry on foot into the park is with licensed nature guides (operator sources describe this as mandatory).

logistics.notes: Park HQ at Thakurdwara. Far fewer visitors than Chitwan (26,131 visitors in FY 2023-24).

highlights: Estimated 125 tigers in Bardia and adjoining forests (2022 survey) - Nepal's second-largest tiger population after Chitwan (128)
On-foot tiger tracking with naturalist guides
Wild elephants (park estimate ~120), one-horned rhino (38 in 2021 count), swamp deer, blackbuck
Gangetic dolphin, gharial and mugger crocodile on the Karnali
230 bird species incl. Bengal florican and sarus crane (NTB)
risks: Dangerous wildlife on walking safaris (tiger, wild elephant, rhino)

acclimatization.notes: Lowland Terai park; no altitude concerns.

unverified: NTB's Bardiya destination page still lists an older fee of NPR 1,000 per day for foreigners; the NTB park-fee table and Kathmandu Post (March 2025, quoting park officials) give NPR 1,500 per entry - the latter is used.
Mandatory licensed nature guide for walking in Bardia is stated by operators, not checked against a park regulation.
Best tiger-sighting months (Mar-May) are operator claims.
